edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: De coelo descendet civitas in anastasi prima: Est quod referamus de fabrica tanta coelesti. Resurgemus illi qui fuimus illi devoti, Et incorrupti erunt, jam tunc sine morte viventes: Sed nec dolor ullus, nec gemitus erit in illa. Venturi sunt illi quoque sub Antichristo qui vincunt Robusta martyria: et ipsi toto tempore vivunt, Recipiuntque bona quoniam mala passi fuere, Et generant ipsi per annos mille nubentes. Comparantur ibi tota vectigalia terrae, Terra quia nimium fundit sine fine novata. Inibi non pluvia, non frigus in aurea castra, Obsidiae nullae, sicut nunc, neque rapinae, Nec lucernae lumen desiderat civitas illa: Ex auctore suo lucet, nec non ibi paret Per duodecim millia stadia lata; longa, sic alta; Radicem in terra, sed caput cum coelo peraequat, In urbe pro foribus autem sol et luna lucebit. Malus in angore septus propter justos alendos. Ab annis autem mille Deus omnia perdet.
pass_a_gloss: The city will descend from heaven in the first resurrection: There is what we should report about such a great heavenly structure. We who were devoted will rise again, and they will be incorrupt, already then living without death: But neither will any pain, nor any groaning be in that place. Those also who will come under the Antichrist, who overcome strong martyrdoms, will live for the whole time, and will receive good things because they suffered evil, and they themselves will produce offspring for a thousand years while marrying. All the revenues of the earth are compared there, because the earth, renewed without end, pours out an abundance. There will be no rain, no cold in the golden camp, no sieges, as now, nor plunderings, nor will the city desire the light of lamps: It shines from its author, and also there it will be visible, for it is wide through twelve thousand stadia, long, and equally high; it has its root on the earth, but its head equals the heaven, and in the city, instead of doors, the sun and the moon will shine. The evil one is shut up in anguish on account of the just being nourished. But from the thousand years, God will destroy all things.

choices.why: referring to God as the source of light
referring to the opponent of Christ
referring to the enemy of God

pass_b_english: The city will descend from heaven at the first resurrection, and we must speak of so great a heavenly structure. We who were devoted will rise again, incorruptible, already living without death; neither pain nor groaning will exist there. Those who come under the Antichrist and overcome severe martyrdoms will also live for the whole period, receiving good things because they suffered evil, and they themselves will produce offspring for a thousand years while marrying. All the revenues of the earth are matched there, because the endlessly renewed earth pours out abundance. No rain, no cold will touch the golden camp; no sieges as now, no plundering; the city will not need lamplight, for it shines from its Author and will be visible across twelve thousand stadia wide, long, and equally high — its root on earth, its head level with heaven — and in the city, instead of gates, the sun and moon will shine. The Evil One is shut up in anguish for the sake of feeding the just. But after the thousand years God will destroy all things (Revelation 20:1-6).

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A preserves the clause structure and nuances (e.g., 'nuptiales' implied by 'nubentes' as 'while marrying'). Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains the meaning of Pass A and the source. The scripture citation (Revelation 20:1-6) in Pass B correctly identifies the theological allusion to the millennium and the first resurrection present in the text.

source: 'De coelo descendet civitas in anastasi prima: Est quod referamus de fabrica tanta coelesti.', english: 'The city will descend from heaven at the first resurrection, and we must speak of so great a heavenly structure.'
